observation_kind: 140 distinct official-source checks plus 12 exact-data blockers; each check applied once to 3 preserved candidates; no validation-mode multiplication.
f: A monthly INSPIRE release contains data from the previous month.
A published INSPIRE release remains available until the following monthly release.
A polygon crossing a local-authority boundary can appear in both authority files.
The index map can be searched to determine whether land is registered.
Business e-services users can use MapSearch to view the full Index Polygon dataset.
MapSearch access to the full Index Polygon dataset is described as free for business e-services customers.
Failure to comply with OGL conditions ends the reuse rights automatically.
Reuse requires the HM Land Registry attribution statement.
Reuse of polygon geometry also requires the Ordnance Survey attribution statement.
Reusers should link to the INSPIRE conditions where possible.
The guidance identifies conversion from GML to KML for Google Maps.
QGIS is identified as a free open-source tool for viewing and converting GML.
The required GML conversion depends on the target GIS system and format.
The q parameter can search by postcode.
The typology parameter accepts an array of typology values.
organisation_entity filters entities managed by specified organisations.
The entity parameter accepts one or more entity numbers.
The curie parameter accepts one or more CURIE values.
The prefix parameter accepts one or more prefixes.
The reference parameter accepts one or more references.
The period parameter can select current or all entries.
start_date_year filters entities by start-date year.
start_date_month filters entities by start-date month.
start_date_day filters entities by start-date day.
A longitude point filter requires latitude.
A latitude point filter requires longitude.
The geometry parameter can accept one or more WKT geometries.
geometry_reference can spatially filter using entities with specified references.
geometry_curie can spatially filter using entities matching specified CURIEs.
The limit parameter controls the number of returned results.
The offset parameter defines where entity pagination begins.
The field parameter accepts multiple requested response fields.
field selections take precedence over exclude_field selections.
The quality parameter accepts one or more quality filters.
Single-entity retrieval requires an integer entity identifier.
Single-entity retrieval supports JSON, HTML and GeoJSON.
The dataset-list endpoint can filter by dataset slug.
The dataset-list endpoint supports field selection.
The dataset-list endpoint supports field exclusion.
include_typologies can remove typologies from dataset JSON when set false.
Dataset-detail retrieval requires a dataset slug.
Dataset-detail retrieval supports JSON and HTML.
Planning applications can be filtered using a start date and a since match.
The planning-application specification is described as still in development.
Local planning authorities are not currently required to share application data to that specification.
Spaces in custom WKT query strings must be percent-encoded.
Pagination advances offset by the selected limit.
Portfolio request loops should apply polite rate limiting.
Parquet is identified as suitable for large datasets.
Listed-building entities include a listed_building_grade field.
A published endpoint may be a hosted file or a live API feed.
Each published record needs a documentation-url.
Records representing legal documents need a direct document-url.
A 1m DSM survey has an average point density of at least one point per square metre.
A 50cm DSM survey has an average point density of four points per square metre.
A 25cm DSM survey has an average point density of sixteen points per square metre.
Published point-density figures are calculated for the DSM.
The DSM density basis uses the last or only laser return.
DTM point density beneath vegetation may be lower than the nominal DSM density.
Point density varies across the scan.
Overlap from multiple flight lines can increase point density.
Terrain changes can affect density in the forward scan direction.
The point cloud is not a regular grid.
The composite delivery changed from ASCII to GeoTIFF.
The GeoTIFF transition covered both 1m and 2m composite products.
Composite GeoTIFFs are supplied in 5km tiles.
Composite GeoTIFF elevations are stored in metres.
GeoTIFF is described as an open geospatial standard.
GeoTIFF data volumes are reported as about five times smaller than ASCII.
Reduced GeoTIFF volumes enable faster internet downloads.
Reduced GeoTIFF volumes make storage more manageable.
GeoTIFF enables web services such as WCS and image services.
The GeoTIFF format aligns Composite products with National LIDAR Programme products.
QGIS is listed as able to open the GeoTIFF files.
ArcGIS is listed as able to open the GeoTIFF files.
GRASS is listed as able to open the GeoTIFF files.
AutoCAD Civil3D is listed as able to open the GeoTIFF files.
Survey download spatial metadata indexes are now supplied as GeoPackage.
The GeoPackage index describes the spatial location of raster data.
The GeoPackage index describes the temporal extent of raster data.
LIDAR point clouds are supplied in LAZ format.
LAZ is identified as the compressed form of LAS.
Survey raster tile size depends on source resolution.
Very large selected areas may require a Large Data Request.
Browser pop-ups must be enabled for the Download All function.
WMS provides a summarised representation of elevation data.
WCS provides elevation coverage values rather than only rendered imagery.
Composite service endpoints removed the release-year suffix.
Updated composite endpoints distinguish first and last return products.
The no-year service endpoint is intended to remain persistent across future updates.
The publisher acknowledges compatibility issues with WCS in ArcGIS.
ArcGIS WCS does not automatically support raster statistics.
ArcGIS users may need a stretch render for WCS elevation rasters.
WCS GeoTIFF NoData is represented by a numeric floating-point sentinel.
DSP states that it will adopt OGC APIs as they become available.
OS Terrain 50 XML metadata follows the GEMINI metadata standard.
Metadata is provided for national sets and individual tiles.
The XML includes comments explaining tag meanings.
Metadata records whether content is grid DTM or vector contours.
Metadata records the 10km National Grid tile reference.
Metadata identifies the INSPIRE topic category as elevation.
Metadata identifies British National Grid using EPSG:27700.
Metadata identifies Ordnance Datum Newlyn using EPSG:5701.
Tile metadata records the earliest flying date present.
Tile metadata records the latest flying date present.
Earliest and latest flying dates may be identical.
Profile content records Date Flown as null.
The processing date is tile creation date, not the real-world survey date.
Tile metadata includes an incrementing publication version number.
Metadata distinguishes creation from revision or verification.
Lineage can state that a tile was created from new imagery.
Lineage can state that parts were revised from new imagery.
Lineage can state that new imagery was examined and no change found.
An XSLT stylesheet converts metadata XML to HTML for browser viewing.
Some connected software can load the referenced stylesheet automatically.
The ASC auxiliary XML contains minimum, maximum, mean and standard-deviation heights.
The styling statistics are supplied with the same values for every tile.
The auxiliary statistics support consistent colour ramps across adjacent tiles.
Default styling can be disabled by removing the auxiliary XML.
Default styling can also be changed by adjusting minimum and maximum values.
The official known-issues page reports no live OS Terrain 50 issues.
Resolved issue details remain listed until the next product release.
Unlisted product issues can be reported through OS contact channels.
The downloads page provides an XML schema resource for contour products.
The downloads page provides an XML schema resource for gridded products.
The downloads page provides a viewing-style metadata schema resource.
Use of OS XML schemas is governed by the XML File Repository Licence.
OS Terrain 50 download is available without registration.
The tiled national supply is arranged into 55 folders.
Each supply folder represents a 100km National Grid square.
GeoPackage contour data is provided as one national flat file.
Vector-tile contour data is provided as one national flat file.
Grid and contour supplies are delivered in separate compressed folders.
OS recommends using a download manager for tiled supplies.
The tiled zip compression is not encrypted.
Updates are delivered by annual full-tile resupply.
A full national grid supply is approximately 157 MB compressed.
The official refresh schedule lists OS Terrain 50 annually in July.
b: HMLR_EXACT_HARINGEY_GML_REDIRECT
The exact Haringey GML download still enters a redirect loop in the web client.
HMLR_EXACT_HARINGEY_GML_BYTES_SHA256
Exact current Haringey GML bytes and SHA-256 were not captured.
HMLR_NATIVE_BNG_CONTAINMENT
Native-BNG polygon containment was not established for the three candidates.
HMLR_INSPIRE_ID_TITLE_BINDING
No exact current INSPIRE ID-to-title binding was read back.
PLANNING_EXACT_COORDINATE_RESPONSES
The three candidate coordinate responses remained blocked by the web URL-safety gate.
PLANNING_AUTHORITATIVE_CONTAINMENT
No authoritative Planning Data geometry containment was established for the candidates.
EA_WCS_CAPABILITIES_XML_PARSE
The WCS capabilities response is XML and was not parsed by the web client.
EA_TQ2892_WCS_BYTES_SHA256
Exact TQ2892 WCS GeoTIFF bytes and SHA-256 were not captured.
EA_CANDIDATE_NUMERIC_PIXELS
No candidate elevation pixel was read from authenticated raster bytes.
OS_PRODUCTS_JSON_EXACT_READBACK
The exact live OS products JSON response was not captured in this environment.
OS_TQ29_ARCHIVE_BYTES_SHA256
Exact current TQ29 archive bytes and SHA-256 were not captured.
OS_TQ29_CELL_VALUES
The two target Terrain 50 cell values were not read back.
